arxiv-1804-00987.title: A Language for Function Signature Representations
arxiv-1804-00987.creator: Kyle Richardson
arxiv-1804-00987.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Kyle Richardson. Recent work by ( Richardson and Kuhn 2017a ; Richardson and Kuhn 2017b ; Richardson et al. 2018 ) looks at semantic parser induction and question answering in the domain of source code libraries and APIs. In this brief note, we formalize the representations being learned in these studies and introduce a simple domain specific language and a systematic translation from this language to first-order logic.

arxiv-2104-11804.title: Higher-Order Corrections to the Bubble-Nucleation Rate at Finite Temperature
arxiv-2104-11804.creator: Andreas Ekstedt , a
arxiv-2104-11804.description: Abstract In this paper I discuss how to consistently incorporate higher-order corrections to the bubble-nucleation rate at finite temperature. Doing so I examine the merits of different approaches, with the goal of reducing uncertainties for gravitational-wave calculations. To be specific, the region of applicability and accuracy of the derivative expansion is discussed.

Affiliation: Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology, Mosc
arxiv-2106-14092.creator: Dmitry Pasechnyuk
arxiv-2106-14092.description: Abstract This paper discusses the problem of maximizing the total data transmission utility of the computer network. The total utility is defined as the sum of the individual (corresponding to each node in the network) utilities that are concave functions of the data transmission rate.

arxiv-2203-08338.creator: Roberts, Amy, Tunnell, Christopher, von Krosigk, Belina, Anderson, Tyler, Brodsky, Jason, Buuck, Micah, Cartaro, Tina, Cragin, Melissa, Davies, Gavin S, Diamond, Miriam, Fan, Alden, Higuera, Aaron, Ippolito, Valerio, Jillings, Chris, Kravitz, Scott, Krezko, Luke, Li, Ivy, Monzani, Maria Elena, Ostro
arxiv-2203-08338.description: Abstract 1 Abstract This paper summarizes the needs of the dark matter and neutrino communities as it relates to computation. The scope includes data acquisition, triggers, data management and processing, data preservation, simulation, machine learning, data analysis, software engineering, career development, and equity and inclusion.

arxiv-2204-06090.title: Unique Optima of the Delsarte Linear Program
arxiv-2204-06090.creator: Rupert Li
arxiv-2204-06090.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Rupert Li. The Delsarte linear program is used to bound the size of codes given their block length n n and minimal distance d d by taking a linear relaxation from codes to quasicodes.

arxiv-2206-07811.title: Safety Guarantees for Neural Network Dynamic Systems via Stochastic Barrier Functions
arxiv-2206-07811.creator: Rayan Mazouz, Karan Muvvala, Akash Ratheesh, Luca Laurenti, Morteza Lahijanian
arxiv-2206-07811.description: Abstract Neural Networks (NNs) have been successfully employed to represent the state evolution of complex dynamical systems. Such models, referred to as NN dynamic models (NNDMs), use iterative noisy predictions of NN to estimate a distribution of system trajectories over time. Despite their accuracy, safety analysis of NNDMs is known to be a challenging problem and remains largely unexplored.

arxiv-2209-02028.title: Evaluation of the Region of Attractions of Higher Dimensional Hyperbolic Systems using the Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition
arxiv-2209-02028.creator: C. Garcia-Tenorio, D. Tellez-Castro, E. Mojica-Nava, A. Vande Wouwer
arxiv-2209-02028.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by C. Garcia-Tenorio, D. Tellez-Castro, E. Mojica-Nava, A. Vande Wouwer. This paper proposes an original methodology to compute the regions of attraction in hyperbolic and polynomial nonlinear dynamical systems using the eigenfunctions of the discrete-time approximation of the Koopman operator given by the extended dynamic mode decomposition algorithm. The proposed method relies on the spectral decomposition of the Koopman operator to build eigenfunctions that capture the boundary of the region of attraction.

arxiv-2305-14813.title: Semi-Supervised and Long-Tailed Object Detection with CascadeMatch Journal: IJCV
arxiv-2305-14813.creator: Yuhang Zang, Kaiyang Zhou, Chen Huang, Chen Change Loy
arxiv-2305-14813.description: Abstract This paper focuses on long-tailed object detection in the semi-supervised learning setting, which poses realistic challenges, but has rarely been studied in the literature. We propose a novel pseudo-labeling-based detector called CascadeMatch. Our detector features a cascade network architecture, which has multi-stage detection heads with progressive confidence thresholds.

arxiv-2306-12438.creator: Shenghuan Sun University of California, San Francisco shenghuan.sun@ucsf.edu, Gregory M. Goldgof Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center goldgofg@mskcc.org Atul ButteUniversity of California, San Francisco atul.butte@ucsf.edu Ahmed M. AlaaUniversity of California, Berkeley amalaa@berkeley.edu
arxiv-2306-12438.description: Abstract Generative models capable of capturing nuanced clinical features in medical images hold great promise for facilitating clinical data sharing, enhancing rare disease datasets, and efficiently synthesizing annotated medical images at scale. Despite their potential, assessing the quality of synthetic medical images remains a challenge.

arxiv-2508-04349.title: GTPO and GRPO-S: Token and Sequence-Level Reward Shaping with Policy Entropy
arxiv-2508-04349.creator: Hongze Tan Jianfei Pan
arxiv-2508-04349.description: Abstract Reinforcement learning (RL) with algorithms like Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) improves Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning, but is limited by a coarse-grained credit assignment that applies a uniform reward to all tokens in a sequence. This is a major flaw in long-chain reasoning tasks. This paper solves this with Dynamic Entropy Weighting .

arxiv-2510-03619.title: Broadband Quantum Photon Source in Step-Chirped Periodically Poled Lithium Niobate Waveguide
arxiv-2510-03619.creator: Xiao-Xu Fang, Guoliang Shentu, He Lu
arxiv-2510-03619.description: Abstract Broadband nonlinear optical devices play a critical role in both classical and quantum optics. Here, we design and fabricate a 6.82-mm-long step-chirped periodically poled lithium niobate (CPPLN) waveguide on lithium niobate on insulator, which enables quasi-phase matching over a broad bandwidth for second-harmonic generation (SHG) and spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC). The SHG achieves an average efficiency of 54.

arxiv-2510-19601.creator: Martín Matamala
arxiv-2510-19601.description: Abstract In 2008 Chen and Chvátal conjectured that any metric space on n n points has at least n n lines, unless all the points belong to one line. Chvátal proved in 2014 that this is indeed the case for metric spaces with distances 0 0 , 1 1 and 2 2 .

britannica-1911-valentinus-and-the-valen.title: Valentinus and the Valentinians (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-valentinus-and-the-valen.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-valentinus-and-the-valen.description: Article 'Valentinus and the Valentinians' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 27), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. The authorities which we have to consider deal for the most part with Valentinianism in its fully developed form, and not with the original teaching of the master. Justin’s Syntagma (v.s.), which treats of Valentinus, is unfortunately lost. Irenaeus in his section i. 11, 1—3, has preserved what is obviously an older document, possibly from Justin, dealing with Valentinus’s own teaching and that of two of his disciples.

pmc-11364614.title: COVID-19 pandemic-related drugs and microplastics from mask fibers jointly affect soil functions and processes
pmc-11364614.creator: Jeane dela Cruz, Daniel Lammel, Shin Woong Kim, Mohan Bi, Matthias Rillig
pmc-11364614.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The COVID-19 pandemic has led to an unprecedented increase in pharmaceutical drug consumption and plastic waste disposal from personal protective equipment. Most drugs consumed during the COVID-19 pandemic were used to treat other human and animal diseases. Hence, their nearly ubiquitous presence in the soil and the sharp increase in the last 3 years led us to investigate their potential impact on the environment. Similarly, the compulsory use of face masks has led to an enormous amount of plastic waste.

pmc-11594307.title: Parasiticidal Properties of Nanoemulsion-Based Plant Essential Oil Formulations for Controlling Poultry Ectoparasites in Farm Conditions
pmc-11594307.creator: Jarongsak Pumnuan, Anuwat Lakyat, Ampon Klompanya, Duangkamol Taemchuay, Amorn Assavawongsanon, Thanaporn Doungnapa, Somsak Kramchote, Ian R Dadour
pmc-11594307.description: Simple SummaryThis study evaluates nanoemulsion-based plant essential oil formulations (NEOFs) containing clove and cinnamon oils for controlling poultry ectoparasites in farm conditions. The results showed that NEOFs achieved an over 95% ectoparasite eradication after two treatments, compared to significantly higher levels in untreated controls.

pmc-12549711.title: The dark side of avocados: a review of anthracnose and stem-end rot in postharvest fruit
pmc-12549711.creator: Valentina Valencia Bernal, Nathanial J. Boeckman, Srđan G. Aćimović, Fatemeh Khodadadi
pmc-12549711.description: Avocados are a key global fruit crop with rising international demand. However, postharvest diseases like anthracnose and stem-end rot (SER) can lead to significant economic losses, with incidence rates surpassing 30% in some regions. The latent nature of these infections complicates detection and management, affecting fruit quality and marketability.

pmc-12551332.title: Impacts of different dietary soybean meal levels on jejunal immunity of nursery pigs at different days post-weaning
pmc-12551332.creator: Hyunjun Choi, Zixiao Deng, Sung Woo Kim
pmc-12551332.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe objective of this study was to investigate the impacts of different dietary soybean meal (SBM) levels on jejunal immunity in nursery pigs at different days post-weaning.MethodsForty-eight pigs (6.2 ± 0.3 kg), weaned at 21 days of age, were assigned to 2 dietary treatments (n = 12) in a randomized complete block design and fed for 20 or 42 d in 3 phases (10, 10, and 22 d, respectively). The dietary treatments consisted of low and high SBM diets.

Despite its serious threat to public health, effective therapeutic strategies that simultaneously target T3SS effectors and biofilm remain underdeveloped. In this study, we deleted the hslV gene in S.

pmc-12606254.title: Training human super-recognizers’ detection and discrimination of AI-generated faces
pmc-12606254.creator: Katie L H Gray, Josh P Davis, Carl Bunce, Eilidh Noyes, Kay L Ritchie
pmc-12606254.description: Generative adversarial networks (GANs) can create realistic synthetic faces, which have the potential to be used for nefarious purposes. The synthetic faces produced by GANs are difficult to detect and are often judged to be more realistic than real faces. Training programmes have been developed to improve human synthetic face detection accuracy, with mixed results.

pmc-13146034.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A810 IMPACT OF LOW SYSTOLIC BLOOD PRESSURE ON PERIVENTRICULAR WHITE MATTER HYPERINTENSITIES IN ELDERLY PATIENTS WITH CONTROLLED HYPERTENSION
pmc-13146034.creator: Elsayed Abed
pmc-13146034.description: Background and aimsBoth high and low blood pressure can contribute to cerebral white matter hyperintensities (WMH). However, the effect of hypotension in patients with treated hypertension is unclear. This study examined the association between low blood pressure and WMH volume and location in elderly patients with controlled hypertension compared to those without hypertension.

pmc-13312402.title: Prognostic models for predicting intensive care unit admission or mortality in critically ill adults not yet been admitted to the intensive care unit
pmc-13312402.creator: Aléxia Gabriela Silva Vieira, Ana Carolina Pereira Nunes Pinto, Amanda Alves Assis Garcia, Ricardo Kenji Nawa, Caroline Gomes Mól, Josué DR Duenas, Álvaro N Atallah, Gentle S Shrestha, Marcus J Schultz, Humberto Saconato, Virginia FM Trevisani

The objectives are as follows:To determine whether prognostic models can be used for predicting the occurrence of ICU admission and mortality within the index hospital admission, and post‐discharge survival at reported follow‐up time points, up to one year, in critically ill adults not yet admitted to the ICU.

pmc-13360018.title: Clinical Impact of a Germline CD19 Variant on Treatment Outcome After CAR-T Cell Therapy in Relapsed/Refractory Mantle Cell Lymphoma
pmc-13360018.creator: Simona Andrea Ruckstuhl, Katja Seipel, Inna Shaforostova, Martina Bertschinger, Ulrike Bacher, Thomas Pabst
pmc-13360018.description: Simple SummaryDespite therapeutic advances, mantle cell lymphoma remains an incurable disease. CD19-directed CAR-T cell therapy can induce durable responses in patients with relapsed or refractory mantle cell lymphoma, but outcomes vary considerably. Germline variants of the CD19 gene may contribute to a heterogeneous response.

pmc-13382803.title: Reconsidering the usefulness of using long-acting injectable buprenorphine as a tapering tool: a case report of delayed withdrawal months after last dose
pmc-13382803.creator: Kareem Woods, Sophia Graham, Steven Dobscha, Christopher Blazes
pmc-13382803.description: BackgroundLong-acting injectable buprenorphine (LAIB) has generated enthusiasm as a potential tapering strategy for patients seeking discontinuation from buprenorphine therapy. The rationale is pharmacokinetic: gradual decline in plasma concentrations over months may blunt or prevent withdrawal. Yet protocols, clinical risks, and the characteristics of delayed withdrawal during LAIB tapers are poorly described.

pmc-13583851.title: Feasibility, use and usability of an adapted mHealth tool for dementia risk reduction among middle-aged and older adults in Germany: protocol for a non-randomised pilot study
pmc-13583851.creator: Andrea E Zülke, Melanie Luppa, Kay Deckers, Sebastian Köhler, Steffi G Riedel-Heller
pmc-13583851.description: IntroductionSeveral potentially modifiable factors are associated with the risk of cognitive decline and dementia, indicating potential for risk reduction via lifestyle modifications. While multidomain interventions targeting lifestyle changes for dementia risk reduction are often highly selective and resource-intensive, eHealth/mHealth interventions offer a potentially low-cost, scalable approach to promote brain-healthy lifestyles for a large number of individuals.
